nodes.name: iso6346.ts
nodes.summary: ISO 6346 container-number toolkit: normalizes and validates the owner-code/serial format, computes the standard check digit from the letter-value mapping, and ranks typo-correction suggestions for near-miss container numbers.

nodes.name: normalizeContainerNumber
nodes.summary: Strips dashes and whitespace from a container number and uppercases it for canonical comparison.

nodes.name: validateContainerFormat
nodes.summary: Checks that a container number matches the ISO 6346 owner-code (3 letters + category letter) and 6-digit serial format.

nodes.name: calculateCheckDigit
nodes.summary: Computes the ISO 6346 check digit by summing letter-mapped values weighted by powers of two and mapping the sum modulo 11 onto the standard digit sequence.

nodes.name: validateCheckDigit
nodes.summary: Verifies that a full 11-character container number's trailing check digit matches the recomputed ISO 6346 value.

nodes.name: validateContainerNumber
nodes.summary: Full container-number validation combining format and check-digit checks, returning a structured result instead of a bare boolean.

nodes.name: suggestCorrections
nodes.summary: Ranks up to maxResults typo corrections for an invalid container number by mutating single digits (and owner letters) and scoring candidates whose recomputed check digit validates, preferring mutations closest to the original.

nodes.name: computeVehicleAlerts

nodes.name: fuelSurcharge.ts
nodes.summary: Computes the customer fuel surcharge when the current fuel price exceeds the contractual base price, splitting the delta by the customer's share percentage over a quota in liters. Returns a zero/non-applicable result whenever any price, share, or quota input is missing or the precondition fails.

nodes.name: computeFuelSurcharge
nodes.summary: Calculates the surcharge as (currentPrice − basePrice) × quotaLiters × sharePct/100, rounded to 2dp then to a whole number via roundInt. Guards against null prices/share, non-positive share or quota, and currentPrice ≤ basePrice by returning { amount: 0, applicable: false }.

nodes.name: computeFreightRate
nodes.summary: Calculates whole-VND base freight including revenue share plus a fuel-price-difference surcharge clamped to zero, rounding intermediates to two decimals before whole-unit rounding.

nodes.name: round.ts
nodes.summary: Shared rounding helpers: symmetric decimal-place rounding through scientific notation and nonnegative nearest-integer rounding for whole fuel liters. Decimal ties round away from zero, not banker half-even rounding.

nodes.name: round2dp
nodes.summary: Rounds to two decimal places using scientific-notation shifting and symmetric sign handling; half ties round away from zero.

nodes.name: roundInt
nodes.summary: Rounds to the nearest integer and clamps negative results to zero for whole-liter and whole-amount calculations.

nodes.name: tripTotals.ts
nodes.summary: Core trip P&L engine shared by backend and frontend: resolves fuel liters by precedence (FLAT_RATE override → fixed route allowance → per-leg AUTO norms), computes fuel cost with actual-vs-standard price variance, road allowance, net VETC toll cost with kẹp-hàng backhaul dedup, VAT-aware freight ex-VAT and recorded revenue after commission, and splits cost/profit math between OWN and EXTERNAL carrier types.

nodes.name: computeRoadAllowance
nodes.summary: Derives the driver road allowance: when tollsAddition is positive it replaces the base rate entirely (plus return-cargo bonus), otherwise it uses base − (toll stations × per-station toll) + bonus; subtracts tollsDiscount and clamps the result at zero.

nodes.name: computeTripTotals
nodes.summary: Main trip totals function: resolves fuel liters by precedence (FLAT_RATE → fixed mountain/route allowance → per-leg km×norm) with whole-liter rounding, then assembles the P&L — fuel cost at the effective price (actual ?? standard) with variance tracking, road allowance honoring manual override, net toll cost (gross − kẹp-hàng tollDeduction clamped ≥ 0), freightExVat/recordedRevenue after VAT and customer commission, and the OWN (fuel+allowance+tolls+salary+bonuses) vs EXTERNAL (incl-VAT freight cost only) cost branches.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Allowlist-style Docker build-context filter for the backend image: excludes everything with a root `*`, then re-includes only the pnpm workspace manifests, shared/backend sources, and Drizzle migration files that backend/Dockerfile actually COPYs, keeping the root context intact so pnpm workspace links still resolve.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusion list that strips node_modules, VCS/agent-tool state, test and QA artifacts, dist builds, backend tests, drizzle migration snapshots, docs/plans, and all env files from image builds, keeping only README.md and .env.example as negation exceptions.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: The repository's binding agent contract: strict trunk-based git workflow (no branches, worktrees, or PRs), closed-loop SDLC with mandatory QA gates (lint, typecheck, backend/frontend tests, build, E2E), testplan-first regression rules for user-reported bugs, and a strict UI-verification claim ladder that forbids calling anything tested without browser-interaction evidence.

nodes.name: CONTEXT.md
nodes.summary: Compact development-context entrypoint defining the authority order for conflicting sources, the repository shape (shared contracts/calculations, Express+Drizzle backend, React frontend, e2e, docs/prd, deploy), core invariants (Drizzle-only SQL policy, round2dp financial math, JWT+Casbin gating), and the progressive context-loading protocol with dev endpoints.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Root orchestration for the entire dev/deploy lifecycle: boots the local stack (compose up, backup-first drizzle migrations, backend :3001 + vite :7174), database utilities (timestamped pg_dump backups, serialized migration generation with a schema-drift guard, prod/staging-to-dev and prod-to-staging DB sync), and the two deploy pipelines — make demo (staging, :latest channel) and make deploy (prod branch AS-IS, :prod channel) — each with rollback image capture, server-side DB backup, flock-serialized migrate, cutover, and public health checks.

nodes.summary: Manifest for the @tingting/backend ESM workspace package: defines the dev/build/test/seed script chain (tsx watch, tsc via tsconfig.build.json followed by an ESM import fix, drizzle-kit db commands, prod seeding) and pins runtime dependencies including Express 5, Drizzle ORM, Casbin, OpenTelemetry, pino, and zod.

nodes.name: tsconfig.build.json
nodes.summary: Production build TypeScript config that extends the backend's base tsconfig.json and excludes tests (src/tests, *.test.ts, *.spec.ts) so the `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` build emits only runtime code into dist.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Base TypeScript config for the backend package: extends the monorepo-root tsconfig.base.json, emits to dist with src as rootDir, and enables incremental builds with a .tsbuildinfo cache; includes all of src for dev-time typechecking.

nodes.name: docker-compose.prod.yml
nodes.summary: Staging Docker Compose stack for vantai.tingting.vip with project name vantai: pgvector Postgres16, Redis7, backend/frontend on the latest image channel, dedicated /opt/vantai data volumes and opt-in localhost Adminer. The real production stack is docker-compose.silversea.yml.

nodes.name: docker-compose.silversea.yml
nodes.summary: Production Docker Compose stack for silversea.tingting.vip (project 'silversea'), pinned to the :prod image channel so demo deploys can never clobber prod. It owns dedicated data volumes under /opt/silversea/data that deploys never touch, and is driven by the root Makefile's PROD_COMPOSE target (`make deploy`), which only recreates backend/frontend.

nodes.name: seed-staging-2026-08-05-customer-sites.sql
nodes.summary: Staging hotfix for the empty factory dropdown (DEF-20260804-002): upserts operational sites for Bien Bac (factory + warehouse), XNK Ha Noi (ICD warehouse + Bac Son factory), and a Long Minh smoke-test factory, mirroring the backend TypeScript seeder committed in 6d2c0bd.

nodes.name: seed-staging-quytrinh-sites.sql
nodes.summary: Deferred staging seed that upserts 8 Long Minh operational sites from the customer's DATA PM Excel — 3 NEWEB warehouses (Ha Nam/Ninh Binh), 2 ASKEY factories, SUNRISE, SJ Tech, and S-CONNECT (Bac Ninh) — each with Google Maps links, lift-fee invoice details, and driver-facing strict_rules. It requires migration 0170 (operational_sites), so it must be applied only after a backend image redeploy.

nodes.name: seed-staging-quytrinh.sql
nodes.summary: Additive, idempotent staging upsert of real customer master data from the 2026-07-30 Excel delivery: Silver Sea company identity into app_settings, the Long Minh partner/supplier/customer triple (MST 2300540419, 15-day freight payment terms), the 19-column 'MAU DEBIT LONG MINH' debit-note template stored as a JSONB column layout, and a repoint of the khachhang portal user to the Long Minh customer. Preserves existing demo trips and users.

nodes.name: seed-vantai-6months.sql
nodes.summary: Extended variant of the vantai demo seed that spreads the same master data across six months of trips (VT-2601 through VT-2606, almost entirely LOCKED, with trip code counters per month) and randomized created_at/updated_at timestamps — built to exercise monthly reporting, salary-period, and AR-aging screens.

nodes.name: seed-vantai.sql
nodes.summary: Clean-slate demo seed for vantai.tingting.vip: truncates ~35 tables with CASCADE, resets sequences, then loads realistic Vietnamese trucking data — 9 users, 7 trucks, 6 trailers, 6 drivers, 7 suppliers, 10 real logistics customers, 12 Hai Phong routes with JSONB default legs, pricing and road-allowance tables, fuel config, container types, and 14 ports — plus 30 trips across May–June 2026 with legs, forwarder expenses, ledger entries, and vehicle expenses.

nodes.name: setup-silversea-server.sh
nodes.summary: One-time, idempotent provisioning script for the prod server silversea.tingting.vip, run via `make deploy-server-setup`: 11 steps covering DNS sanity, Docker install, /opt/silversea layout, fresh secret generation with shared keys mirrored from the demo .env, compose push, nginx + certbot with a webroot HTTP-01 certificate, auto-renew hooks with a dry-run proof, ufw/SSH hardening, and finally starting postgres + redis for `make deploy` to fill in.

nodes.name: silversea-server-db-backup.sh
nodes.summary: Pre-deploy safety net that pg_dumps the production database via docker exec, discovering POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_DB from the container environment; it aborts the deploy when the dump is suspiciously small on a populated database, keeping the suspect file for inspection.

nodes.name: drizzle.config.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle Kit configuration for the backend: points schema generation at the src/db/schema/index.ts barrel, emits migrations to ./drizzle with the PostgreSQL dialect, and sources the connection URL from DATABASE_URL (defaulting to the local dev Postgres on port 5441).

nodes.name: model.conf
nodes.summary: Casbin authorization model defining a subject/object/action request schema with an allow-if-any policy effect and matchers that honor wildcards ("*" matches any object or action) for backend RBAC enforcement.

nodes.name: policy.csv
nodes.summary: Casbin RBAC policy matrix granting per-role permissions across ~25 resources (trips, shipments, treasury, salary, portals, geotag) for ADMIN, MANAGER, DISPATCHER, ACCOUNTANT, CUS, OPS, DRIVER, and CUSTOMER roles, with inline comments documenting wave-by-wave access decisions such as separating dispatch resources from broad shipment access.

nodes.name: migrate-trailers.ts
nodes.summary: One-off migration script that extracts trailer plates embedded in the trucks table into the standalone trailers table, deduplicating plate/type combinations and re-linking trucks, skipping entirely if trailers already exist.

nodes.name: migrateTrailers
nodes.summary: Transactionally copies unique trailer plate/type combos out of trucks into the trailers table (skipping when rows already exist) and links trucks to the new trailer records.

nodes.name: salary-exclusions.ts
nodes.summary: Salary-period driver exclusion records with period/driver identity, handling choice, actor attribution, follow-up and version metadata.

nodes.name: treasury.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for the treasury/financial-close domain defining six tables: debt offsets, treasury accounts, payment receipts, append-only treasury movements, payment allocations, and payment refunds. Partial unique indexes enforce idempotent posting, single-movement-per-receipt, and single-reversal rules at the database level.

nodes.name: locked-entity-manifest.ts
nodes.summary: Defines executable evidence for terminal financial and operational state protections. References concrete source guards and entity-specific proofs, including direct legacy advance DRAFT recovery without reopening RECORDED or VOIDED history.

nodes.name: role-aliases.ts
nodes.summary: Backward-compatibility layer for the CLERK→CUS and FORWARDER→OPS role rename, canonicalizing legacy role names so auth and RBAC checks keep working with both spellings during the migration period.

nodes.name: canonicalizeRole
nodes.summary: Converts any role string to its canonical modern form (CLERK→CUS, FORWARDER→OPS), passing unknown roles through unchanged.

nodes.name: isLegacyRole
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given role is one of the legacy names (CLERK, FORWARDER) that still needs migration.

nodes.name: getModernRole
nodes.summary: Returns the modern replacement for a legacy role name, or null when the role is already modern or unknown.

nodes.name: areRolesEqual
nodes.summary: Compares two role strings after canonicalization so legacy and modern spellings of the same role compare equal.

nodes.name: getRoleAliasMappings
nodes.summary: Exposes the raw legacy→modern alias mapping for migration tooling and reporting.

nodes.name: telemetry.ts
nodes.summary: OpenTelemetry SDK bootstrap that must be the first import of the server entry point; configures an OTLP or console trace exporter, a ratio-based sampler driven by env vars, and Node auto-instrumentations with signal-hooked flush on shutdown.

nodes.name: readSamplerRatio
nodes.summary: Parses OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG into a 0..1 sampling ratio, rejecting out-of-range or non-finite values.

nodes.name: startSdk
nodes.summary: Builds the OTel resource, exporter, and ratio sampler, starts the NodeSDK with Node auto-instrumentations, and registers SIGTERM/SIGINT hooks that flush and shut down the tracer provider.

nodes.name: customers.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated customer master data from the 2026-07-30 Excel delivery: the LONG MINH customer record with tax codes and payment terms, plus the SilverSea company identity block (address, bank account, representative) used for invoicing.

nodes.name: drivers.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated roster of the customer's real drivers with names, tax codes, hometowns, and phone numbers, extracted from the delivered Excel report forms for seeding the identity tables.

nodes.name: factories.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated factory/receiver master data (NEWEB warehouses and similar) keyed by customer internal code, carrying raw receiver addresses, invoice tax details, driver docking notes, and Google Maps links.

nodes.name: fleet.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated fleet roster pairing heavy truck plates with trailer plates, assigned driver names, payload limits, and preferred-route tags, mirroring the customer's real truck-trailer combinations.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-exporting the generated seed datasets (the Excel-derived ports list and its PortFromExcelSeed type) for the seed modules.

nodes.name: ports-from-excel.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated port seed data (name, address, ops-portal URL, lifting fee) transcribed from the customer's DATA PM Excel workbook; regenerate with tools/generate-seed-data.mjs.

nodes.name: pricing.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated rate-card seed pairing routes with container sizes, revenue-share percentages, base prices, and surcharge-inclusive prices (VND) for the pricing tables.

nodes.name: prod-master-data.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated production master data from the customer's Excel delivery: staff, drivers, customers, sites, routes, tractors, trailers, ports, and carriers as typed constant arrays consumed exclusively by seed-prod.

nodes.name: reference.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated reference data for shipment intake: Hai Phong-area ports with e-port portal URLs, transport routes, and container type catalog.

nodes.name: samples.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated sample trip ledger rows (customer, factory, route, container number, receivable and payable breakdowns including freight, ferry fees, meals, and surcharges) used to seed realistic demo trip data.

nodes.name: vehicles.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated vehicle-class seed from the DATA PM workbook's vehicle-type sheet: license and trailer plates, inspection/license deadlines, per-axle load limits, driver assignments, and preferred routes.

nodes.name: wipe.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the FK-safe business-data wipe for reseeding: a preserved-tables contract (users, push_subscriptions, idempotency_keys are never touched) plus a grouped TRUNCATE ... CASCADE plan/execute pair.

nodes.name: wipeTableList
nodes.summary: Returns the flat list of business tables to wipe from the grouped plan.

nodes.name: planWipe
nodes.summary: Builds the grouped wipe plan used for dry-run output.

nodes.name: executeWipe
nodes.summary: Executes the TRUNCATE ... CASCADE across all business tables on the given database handle.

nodes.name: nginx-frontend.conf
nodes.summary: Nginx server config baked into the frontend Docker image: serves the built SPA with gzip compression, security headers, one-year immutable caching for Vite-hashed static assets, and an index.html fallback for client-side routing.

nodes.name: nginx-host-silversea.conf
nodes.summary: Production TLS reverse proxy for silversea.tingting.vip: /api reaches the backend and other traffic reaches the SPA. Public /uploads is removed in favor of authenticated photo routes; Adminer is available only through an SSH tunnel.

nodes.name: nginx-host-vantai.conf
nodes.summary: Staging TLS reverse proxy for vantai.tingting.vip: routes API and Socket.IO to the backend, the SPA to the frontend, and /adminer to the database GUI. Public /uploads is removed; photo access uses authenticated API routes.

nodes.name: eslint.config.mjs
nodes.summary: Root ESLint config applying typescript-eslint recommended rules to backend and shared sources while explicitly excluding the frontend (it has its own React/TanStack config), generated output, docs, deploy scripts, and all .js/.config files; downgrades no-explicit-any and unused-vars to warnings and allows Express Request type augmentation via declare global.

nodes.name: fifoAging.ts
nodes.summary: FIFO receivable aging with chronological credit application and retained prepayments. Missing debit timestamps fall back to the reference date; open amounts are bucketed as at most30 days,31–60,61–90 and over90 days.

nodes.name: computeFifoAging
nodes.summary: Applies chronological credits to the oldest open debit, carries excess credit to later debits and returns open balances plus whole-VND aging buckets for≤30,31–60,61–90 and>90 days.

nodes.name: tripDriverSalary.ts
nodes.summary: Driver salary allocation helpers that prorate a monthly base salary over trips using a fixed 26-workday divisor (deliberately independent of per-month attendance standardWorkDays), with a fallback to the legacy route-default salary when no base is configured.

nodes.name: computeTripDriverSalary
nodes.summary: Allocates a driver's monthly base salary to a trip as baseSalary / 26 * tripWageDays, rounded to whole VND, returning 0 for non-finite or non-positive inputs.

nodes.name: resolveTripDriverSalary
nodes.summary: Resolves a trip's driver salary by preferring the configured-base allocation and falling back to the legacy route/default salary only when the driver has no usable base salary.

nodes.name: tripFormDefaults.ts
nodes.summary: Canonical fallback constants for trip-form math — fuel price per liter, loaded and empty fuel norms (L/100km), and road allowance per km — extracted from the frontend form so dispatcher calculations, form previews, and accountant P&L all use identical numbers when no fuel/road config is loaded.

nodes.name: api-paths.ts
nodes.summary: Shared typed REST path maps for staff and portal APIs, with parameterized builders for resource identities and nested routes.

nodes.name: driverTaskNote.ts
nodes.summary: Canonical driver-note composition and parsing: known task labels occupy the first semicolon-separated line and free text follows on later lines. Editing preserves whitespace; explicit-save normalization trims manual text and legacy unmatched text remains intact.

nodes.name: composeDriverTaskNote
nodes.summary: Joins nonblank trimmed task labels with semicolons on the first line and appends manual text on a new line without trimming its editing whitespace.

nodes.name: normalizeDriverTaskNote
nodes.summary: Trims the manual-text portion only at explicit save time while preserving a composed tag line; single-line notes are trimmed directly.

nodes.name: parseDriverTaskNote
nodes.summary: Matches exact first-line segments against known tag labels and preserves unmatched segments plus all later lines as manual text, including legacy single-line notes.

nodes.name: source-authority.ts
nodes.summary: Executable source-authority vocabulary for the Q22 business chain: typed catalogs of source/dependent authority kinds, field families, and lock milestones, plus lookup functions deciding which propagation actions (RECOMPUTE, VERSION, ADJUST, REVERSE) are allowed before or after each milestone. Deliberately computes no money and mutates nothing.

nodes.name: findSourceAuthorityPolicy
nodes.summary: Looks up the authority policy row for a (source, dependent) pair from the SOURCE_AUTHORITY_POLICIES list, returning undefined for unknown pairs.

nodes.name: getSourceAuthorityActions
nodes.summary: Returns the allowed propagation actions for a (source, dependent) pair at a given phase (PRE_MILESTONE or POST_MILESTONE), defaulting to an empty list when no policy exists.

nodes.name: isSourceAuthorityActionAllowed
nodes.summary: Boolean gate answering whether a specific action on a (source, dependent) pair is permitted at the given phase — the single check call sites use before propagating a source change.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Public shared-package barrel re-exporting domain types, runtime schemas, labels, calculations, source-authority contracts, navigation and shipment planning for backend and frontend consumers.

nodes.name: pageCatalog.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for SPA page metadata — the canonical path and Vietnamese title for every route (dashboard, dispatch, fleet, finance, config catalogs, driver and forwarder portals, ops field pages) exposed as the typed PAGE_CATALOG constant. Static pages carry literal paths while dynamic pages provide param-based URL builders plus route patterns, deliberately leaving RBAC to App.tsx and Casbin.

nodes.name: app-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Runtime settings contracts for credit thresholds, direct financial authorization limits and salary business-unit scope.

nodes.name: customer-service-finance.ts
nodes.summary: Shared customer-finance, payment, profitability and accounting-register contracts with strict filter/sort schemas and direct-record recoverable-cost eligibility; no new internal decision payload is required.

nodes.name: email-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contract for the ADMIN-only Resend email credential: the API key is write-only (GET responses expose only a masked suffix), and a payload may not both replace and clear the key in the same update.

nodes.name: financial-reporting-policy.ts
nodes.summary: Effective-dated financial reporting policy and truck depreciation profile contracts with strict whole-VND amounts and versioned history for direct authorized changes.

nodes.name: geotag.ts
nodes.summary: Shared wire contract for event-driven photo GPS geotagging: photo-bearing entity types (trip, trip-expense, company-expense photos), fix sources (phone/exif/manual), the POST /api/geotag payload with anti-replay gpsAt and warm-fix diagnostic fields, and the read-shape PhotoGeotag record. Requirements traceability comments tie accuracy/freshness gates to anti-fraud specs.

nodes.name: governance-action.ts
nodes.summary: Legacy-named types and Zod contracts for transient protected-operation adapters. Role capabilities, versions, evidence and audit shapes remain shared; these schemas do not create a persisted approval queue.

nodes.name: ocr-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contract for ADMIN-only OCR settings running on an OpenRouter API key, using the same write-only key semantics as the email settings: GET returns only a masked preview, omitting the key preserves it, and an explicit flag clears it.

nodes.name: shipment-charge-proposal-link.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contract for reviewing shipment charge proposals across five fee fields, discriminated by decision: ACCEPT_LINK must target a specific debit-note document and line with optimistic-concurrency versions, while REJECT requires only a mandatory reason.

nodes.name: work-inbox.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contracts for the role-based work inbox: a common item base (state, parties, blockers, next action, target route) additively extended into operations, driver, customer, accountant, manager, and admin-health projections, plus the paginated response envelope pinned to the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh timezone and the customer delivery-response decision schema that requires a reason on dispute.

nodes.name: shipment-effective.ts
nodes.summary: Pure effective-value resolvers for shipment container planning under the SILVER L1 program contract: factory precedence (container site authority, then shipment site, then legacy free-text factory name) and per-container fulfillment dates cast to the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh business timezone. Every surface that needs the effective factory or planning date resolves through these helpers instead of re-deriving precedence per endpoint.

nodes.name: resolveEffectiveFactory
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective factory for a container through the precedence chain container-level site authority, shipment-level site, then legacy free-text factory name, returning the site id, display label slot, and which level produced the value.

nodes.name: resolveEffectiveFulfillmentDate
nodes.summary: Returns the effective fulfillment/planning date: FCL containers use their appointment cast to the Vietnam local date (allowing sibling containers to plan on different days), falling back to the shipment's expected delivery date.

nodes.name: localDateInBusinessZone
nodes.summary: Casts an ISO instant or Date to its YYYY-MM-DD local date in the +07:00 business timezone via fixed-offset arithmetic, returning null for unparseable input so callers decide between fallback and invalid.

project.name: tingting
project.description: TingTing transport and logistics monorepo: Express5 and Drizzle backend, shared contracts and financial calculations, and Docker deployment infrastructure. The existing graph scope excludes frontend, tests, and product documentation. Generated from the uncommitted working tree; direct recording and online-only requirements apply.

layers.name: API Layer
layers.description: Express 5 route handlers under backend/src/routes (financial, config, trips, shipments, forwarder, portal, salary, OCR, uploads) that translate HTTP requests into service calls behind the auth/Casbin middleware chain.

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: Business services for shipment/dispatch, driver work, direct operational and financial recording, frozen salary and billing snapshots, and transaction-safe corrections. Legacy governance names serve direct protected adapters rather than an internal approval queue.

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: Drizzle schema modules and the shared Postgres client define transport, pricing, company expenses, OPS settlements and confirmed-salary snapshots; database relationship/version/period invariants remain distinct from human approval workflows.

layers.name: Middleware & Security
layers.description: Express middleware chain (JWT auth, Casbin RBAC guard, audit logging, error handler, material-write and forwarder guards) plus the Casbin enforcer singleton with its model.conf/policy.csv policy files.

layers.name: Backend Core
layers.description: HTTP bootstrap, environment validation, structured errors/logs, transaction and cache helpers, scheduler execution and the executable financial-lock manifest.

layers.name: Data Seeding
layers.description: Idempotent seeders under backend/src/seed plus the seed.ts and seed-dashboard.ts entrypoints that populate master data, customers, ports, and AR fixtures into dev and staging databases.

layers.name: Shared Contracts & Calculations
layers.description: The shared/ workspace package consumed by backend and frontend alike: zod contract schemas, financial calculation kernels (round2dp, tripTotals, fuelSurcharge, ISO-6346), constants and API paths, plus the navigation page catalog.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Deployment
layers.description: Multi-stage backend Dockerfile, docker-compose stacks for dev/demo/prod (with their compose service nodes), nginx reverse-proxy configs, server setup and DB backup shell scripts, .dockerignore files, and Makefile deploy pipelines.

tour.title: Start with the product and repository contract
tour.description: Read the project context and agent contract before traversing the transport system. This graph intentionally covers backend, shared contracts and infrastructure; it is not frontend or physical-device verification.

tour.title: Follow an authenticated HTTP request
tour.description: The Express bootstrap mounts role-scoped routes behind JWT, Casbin and audit middleware. Read the material-write registry to see how every mutating endpoint declares its audit/idempotency boundary.

tour.title: Understand durable data and transaction authority
tour.description: The shared Drizzle schema and transaction helpers underpin cross-domain changes. Idempotency records tie a command key to a payload and persisted result so retries cannot silently duplicate a financial action.

tour.title: Read the shared business contracts
tour.description: Backend and frontend consume the same request schemas, lifecycle vocabulary and calculations. These define compact view models separately from money arithmetic and operational date/identity rules.

tour.title: Trace direct shipment planning into dispatch
tour.description: CUS intake and direct container/schedule supplements resolve effective factory and appointment values. Dispatch then assigns transport authority and issues a fulfillment-backed trip under vehicle and source locks.

tour.title: Follow the driver task and delivery evidence
tour.description: Driver read models use canonical route/port data and factory-specific invoice identity. Progress and saved POD evidence are scoped to the driver; terminal tasks cannot be accepted again and physical-document rules remain explicit.

tour.title: Record operations without an approval handoff
tour.description: OPS and forwarder expenses record complete valid entries directly. Settlement finalization checks source ownership, exact totals and evidence; corrections preserve recorded history and apply ledger deltas rather than rewriting it.

tour.title: Separate direct authorization from financial invariants
tour.description: The legacy-named governance adapter executes role, evidence and source-version checks in one request. Ledger, credit-exception, company-expense and billing constraints still prevent duplicate postings, stale corrections and edits to paid/final records.

tour.title: Freeze payroll and official financial snapshots
tour.description: Salary confirmation stores the exact salary and attendance fingerprint. Driver earnings restores that same snapshot and exposes separate later adjustments; billing documents likewise retain official source identity across later operational changes.

tour.title: Inspect runtime delivery and local fixtures
tour.description: Workspace build order compiles shared contracts before their consumers. Docker, backup scripts and seed orchestration support reproducible runtime setup; their presence in this graph does not mean staging/production deployment was performed.
